newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Trucks clog Bucharest to denounce new tax.
newsitem.headline: Trucks clog Bucharest to denounce new tax.

text.p: Hundreds of truck drivers, their horns blaring, brought traffic to a halt in Bucharest on Friday in a protest against a new road tax and government austerity measures.
Four columns of trucks, including fire engines, cranes and cement mixers, converged on the government headquarters at noon before dispersing shortly afterwards.

It was the second consecutive day of trade union protests against the government's cost-cutting measures to introduce market reforms after several months of grace extended to the centrist coalition elected last November.
"The new tax threatens jobs," drivers' union leader Vincentiu Cica said. "Many transport companies will be forced to lay off people and reduce their activity to pay it."

The government this week introduced the road tax but reduced assessments on most vehicles after protests by opposition politicians, motorists and car makers. The revenue is intended to repair the country's potholed highways.
Drivers also demanded increased benefits, including the right to retire at 55, and asked ministers to draw up a strategy to revive the transport sector.
Trade unions have pledged a month of protests to denounce Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea's plans to reduce subsidies, bring prices up to world levels and slim down bloated industry.
Romanian monthly pay is around $60 and official data show that Romanians' purchasing power has been halved since the 1989 collapse of communism.
